subject: Follow-up: competitive evaluation & TCO comparison for Ava Technologies
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood inference — follow-up & TCO comparison

Hi Julia — great chat today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call recap:
- Use case: low-latency customer support summarization + retrieval augmentation (~200ms p50 target).
- Expected workload: ~1.5M generated tokens/day (peak burst), 2.5M embedding tokens/month for search indexes.
- Key evaluation goals: latency under load, local cache/prefix benefits, and unit economics vs hyperscaler endpoints.

High-level competitive frame (we’ll benchmark these in the POC):
- AWS Bedrock (managed); usually higher per-token list price but integrates with other AWS infra.
- Google Vertex/PaLM endpoints; similar managed tradeoffs, sometimes lower latency for short requests.
- Other inference APIs (lower-cost open model hosts) but often lack predictable throughput or observability.

Initial TCO guidance (ballpark per our internal estimates):
- Redwood (hosted) estimated cost: $35 per 1M tokens (generation) assuming 50-token average response and standard batching (batch factor ~8) and 20% cache hit on prefixes.
- AWS Bedrock estimated list cost: $55 per 1M tokens (no batching assumptions).
- Hyperscaler with committed throughput could be lower at scale but requires provisioning and complex routing for fallbacks.

Notes on assumptions: batching = concurrent request grouping (~8x effective throughput), cache hit = prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (20% baseline; expect higher for FAQ-style prompts). We’ll capture detailed logs during the POC to validate these numbers.

Proposed POC plan (attached in PDF and summarized below):
1) Define 3 workload profiles: Synchronous chat (p50 target 200ms), bulk generation (throughput), and embeddings (indexing).
2) Run 48h comparative benchmark: Redwood hosted vs AWS Bedrock vs one other endpoint of your choice.
3) Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, throughput under 95th pct load, per-1M token cost calculated both raw and after batching/cache.
4) Acceptance: p95 < 800ms for chat under realistic burst, and unit cost delta <= 30% vs chosen hyperscaler (or clear degradation reasons).

Attachments: redwood-tco-1m-tokens.xlsx (cost calc), redwood-poc-plan.pdf (detailed steps).

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm POC dates (we suggested May 18–20) and which other provider you want us to benchmark (AWS Bedrock is already in scope).
- Share any internal SLAs or compliance needs (data residency note below).
- Sign the POC SOW (DocuSign link included in attachments) if you want Redwood to provision dedicated capacity for deterministic results.

Data residency: we can run the POC in the us-east-1 region or a VPC-hosted private deploy if you need tighter controls. Happy to loop in our security team.

Thanks again — I’ll set up the HubSpot record and send an updated SOW once you confirm.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-tco-1m-tokens.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Redwood inference — follow-up & TCO comparison

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A few quick items from our side: 
- Confirming we want AWS Bedrock and one additional managed provider in the benchmark (please recommend the second).
- Data residency: production must stay in us-east-1; for the POC we can use us-east-1 as well.
- Metrics: can you add cost-per-conversation alongside per-1M tokens? Our finance team looks at cost per end-user convo.

I’ll check with Samir on availability for the proposed May 18–20 window and get back by EOD.

Julia

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood inference — follow-up & TCO comparison

Appreciate the quick reply, Julia — answered inline and attached an updated spreadsheet with cost-per-conversation. Key updates: 

1) Recommended comparator: Google Vertex (PaLM) — widely comparable and should surface interesting latency differences at short seq lengths. We’ll bench Bedrock + Vertex + Redwood hosted.

2) Cost modeling details added to the spreadsheet (see "assumptions" tab):
- Baseline prompts: avg prompt tokens = 45, avg response tokens = 55 => ~100 tokens per convo.
- Batching: effective batching factor depends on QPS; we modeled conservative (x4) and aggressive (x8).
- Cache hit rate: baseline 20% (FAQ-style prompts), optimistic 40% (high repetition).
- Tokenization differences and model-specific pricing have been normalized to our "token-equivalent" metric in the sheet.

3) Example outputs from the spreadsheet (for readability):
- Redwood hosted (conservative batch x4, 20% cache): ~$140 per 100k conversations (~$1.40 per convo) => translates to ~$35 per 1M tokens as shared.
- Vertex (no-batching baseline): ~$220 per 100k conversations (~$2.20 per convo).

4) POC logistics: 
- If you want deterministic p95 latency numbers we recommend Redwood provisions a small Dedicated pool for the 48h test (SLA-backed), otherwise hosted comparisons will reflect real noisy shared tenancy.
- DocuSign SOW link (placeholder) is in the related links. If you approve we’ll provision and share monitoring dashboards (per-route latency and token breakdown).

Acceptance criteria proposal (updated): p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms for chat, and <=30% delta on cost-per-conversation vs chosen hyperscaler. If Redwood meets latency + cost target, we can scope a 60-day pilot with committed throughput.

Let us know which metrics are highest priority for your finance and infra teams and we’ll add them to the dashboard.

Thanks — I’ll tentatively block the May 18–20 window and send a calendar invite once you confirm.

—Aditya
Attachment: redwood-tco-1m-tokens.xlsx (updated)
